I can't rule out left or right yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.

I can't rule out up or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.
Going left would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going around the edge to (5,2), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes right.
Going around the edge to (5,3), the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,4). So the line goes right.
The line must go around the edge to (5,4): right is number 5, which comes later.
Going left would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going right, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,5). So the line goes up.
Number 4 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going up would force the line onto number 6 before its turn. So the line goes down.
Number 5 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going around the edge to (1,1), the next 8 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,2). So the line goes down.
Going around the edge to (2,1) would leave number 6 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes down.
Number 6 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Cell (5,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Number 8 is only reachable this way.
The line must go around the edge to (1,1): up is number 10, which comes later.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
